tools.markdown-preview.metadata.title: Markdown Preview
tools.markdown-preview.metadata.descript: Write and preview Markdown with a live split-pane editor
tools.markdown-preview.guide.introductio: What Is the Markdown Preview Tool?

The Markdown Preview tool is a free online split-pane editor that lets you write Markdown on the left and see the rendered output on the right in real time. It supports GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM), including tables, task lists, strikethrough, and fenced code blocks.
Whether you are drafting a README for a GitHub repository, writing documentation, composing a blog post, or learning Markdown syntax, this tool gives you instant visual feedback as you type.
tools.markdown-preview.guide.howToUse.ti: How to Use the Markdown Preview Editor
tools.markdown-preview.guide.howToUse.st: Type or paste your Markdown content in the editor pane on the left. The preview pane on the right updates automatically as you type.
Use the formatting toolbar at the top to insert bold, italic, headings, links, images, code blocks, and lists without memorizing syntax.
Click Export HTML to download the rendered output as a standalone HTML file with clean styling.
Click Copy MD to copy your raw Markdown text to the clipboard.
Expand the Markdown Cheat Sheet at the bottom for a quick reference of all supported syntax.
tools.markdown-preview.guide.supportedFe: This editor supports the full CommonMark specification plus GitHub Flavored Markdown extensions. You can use headings (h1 through h6), bold, italic, and strikethrough text, ordered and unordered lists, blockquotes, horizontal rules, inline code and fenced code blocks, links, images, tables with alignment, and task list checkboxes.
tools.markdown-preview.guide.tips.title: Tips for Writing Better Markdown
Use headings hierarchically: start with h1 for the title, h2 for sections, h3 for subsections
Leave a blank line between paragraphs and before/after lists for proper rendering
Use fenced code blocks with a language identifier for syntax highlighting in supported renderers
Preview your content frequently to catch formatting issues early
Use the toolbar buttons to learn the syntax for elements you use less often
tools.markdown-preview.guide.useCases.it: Writing and previewing GitHub README files before committing
Drafting documentation or technical writing in Markdown
Composing blog posts for static site generators like Hugo, Jekyll, or Astro
Learning Markdown syntax with instant visual feedback
Converting Markdown to HTML for embedding in websites or emails
tools.markdown-preview.guide.intro.title: What is a Markdown Preview?
tools.markdown-preview.guide.intro.parag: Markdown Preview is a free online tool for writing and previewing Markdown text. It provides a real-time split-screen editor where you type Markdown on the left and immediately see the rendered output on the right. Everything is processed in your browser.
Type Markdown text in the left editor. Use standard Markdown syntax for formatting: # for headings, **text** for bold, *text* for italics, and [link](url) for links.
The toolbar provides buttons to quickly insert common Markdown elements, including headings, bold, italics, links, images, code blocks, lists, and quotes.
The preview updates in real time in the right pane. Use the copy button to copy the rendered HTML or raw Markdown. Use the download button to save as a .md file.
tools.markdown-preview.faqs.0.question: How do I preview Markdown online?
tools.markdown-preview.faqs.0.answer: Paste or type your Markdown in the editor pane on the left side of this tool. The rendered preview appears instantly on the right side, updating in real time as you make changes.
tools.markdown-preview.faqs.1.question: Does this tool support GitHub Flavored Markdown?
tools.markdown-preview.faqs.1.answer: Yes. The editor fully supports GFM extensions including tables, task lists with checkboxes, strikethrough text, and fenced code blocks. It uses the remark-gfm parser for accurate rendering.
tools.markdown-preview.faqs.2.question: Can I export Markdown as HTML?
tools.markdown-preview.faqs.2.answer: Yes. Click the Export HTML button in the toolbar to download a standalone HTML file with embedded CSS styling. The file is ready to open in any browser or embed in a website.
tools.markdown-preview.faqs.3.question: How do I create a table in Markdown?
tools.markdown-preview.faqs.3.answer: Use pipes (|) to separate columns and hyphens (-) to create the header row divider. For example: | Column 1 | Column 2 | followed by |----------|----------| and then your data rows. The preview pane shows the rendered table instantly.
tools.markdown-preview.faqs.4.question: What is the difference between Markdown and HTML?
tools.markdown-preview.faqs.4.answer: Markdown is a lightweight text formatting syntax that is easier to read and write than HTML. It gets converted to HTML for display. This tool lets you write in Markdown and see the resulting HTML output side by side.
tools.markdown-preview.faqs.5.question: Can I use this editor for GitHub README files?
tools.markdown-preview.faqs.5.answer: Absolutely. This editor supports the same GFM syntax that GitHub uses, so your README will render the same way. Write your content here, preview it, and then copy the Markdown into your repository.
tools.markdown-preview.defaultMarkdown:

tools.image-upscaler.metadata.descriptio: Upscale and enlarge images for free. 2x and 4x scaling with multiple algorithms. No upload, no signup — runs entirely in your browser.
tools.image-upscaler.guide.title: How to use:
tools.image-upscaler.guide.steps.1: Choose scale (2x or 4x) and mode (Smooth, Sharp, or Pixel Art).
tools.image-upscaler.faqs.0.question: How does image upscaling work?
tools.image-upscaler.faqs.0.answer: The tool enlarges your image using advanced canvas interpolation algorithms. Smooth mode uses high-quality bicubic interpolation, Sharp mode applies a sharpening filter after upscaling, and Pixel Art mode uses nearest-neighbor for crisp pixel edges.
tools.image-upscaler.faqs.1.question: Will upscaling make a blurry image sharp?
tools.image-upscaler.faqs.1.answer: Upscaling increases resolution but can't add detail that wasn't in the original image. A small, clear image will upscale well. A blurry or very low-resolution image will remain soft. For best results, start with the highest quality source you have.
tools.image-upscaler.faqs.2.question: What's the maximum upscale size?
tools.image-upscaler.faqs.2.answer: You can upscale up to 4x the original dimensions. For example, a 500x500 image can become 2000x2000. Very large outputs may take a moment to process.
tools.image-upscaler.faqs.3.question: Is my image uploaded anywhere?
tools.image-upscaler.faqs.3.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser using the Canvas API. Your image never leaves your device.
tools.image-upscaler.faqs.4.question: When should I use Pixel Art mode?
tools.image-upscaler.faqs.4.answer: Use Pixel Art (Nearest Neighbor) mode when upscaling pixel art, retro game sprites, or any image where you want to preserve hard pixel edges without blurring or smoothing.
tools.image-upscaler.faqs.5.question: What output formats are available?
tools.image-upscaler.faqs.5.answer: You can download the upscaled image as PNG (lossless, best quality) or JPG (smaller file size). PNG is recommended for graphics and pixel art, JPG for photographs.

tools.image-to-text.metadata.description: Extract text from images for free using OCR. Upload a screenshot, photo, or scanned document and get editable text instantly. No upload, no signup.
tools.image-to-text.guide.title: How to use:
tools.image-to-text.guide.steps.0: Upload an image or paste from clipboard.
tools.image-to-text.guide.steps.1: Choose an engine (PaddleOCR recommended). Optionally select a language for Tesseract.
tools.image-to-text.guide.steps.2: Click "Extract Text" and wait for processing.
tools.image-to-text.guide.steps.3: Copy or download the extracted text.
tools.image-to-text.faqs.0.question: What is OCR?
tools.image-to-text.faqs.0.answer: OCR (Optical Character Recognition) is technology that converts images of text into editable, searchable text. It works on screenshots, photos of documents, scanned pages, and any image containing text.
tools.image-to-text.faqs.1.question: What languages are supported?
tools.image-to-text.faqs.1.answer: The default PaddleOCR engine handles Chinese and English. Switching to the Tesseract engine supports English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Simplified Chinese and Japanese. Select the correct option before processing for best results.
tools.image-to-text.faqs.2.question: Is the text extraction accurate?
tools.image-to-text.faqs.2.answer: Accuracy depends on image quality. Clear, high-contrast text with good resolution gives the best results (95%+ accuracy). Handwritten text, very small fonts, or low-quality images may have lower accuracy.
tools.image-to-text.faqs.3.question: Is my image uploaded to a server?
tools.image-to-text.faqs.3.answer: No. Both OCR engines (PaddleOCR and Tesseract.js) run entirely in your browser. Your images never leave your device. Models are downloaded once and cached.
tools.image-to-text.faqs.4.question: Can I extract text from a PDF?
tools.image-to-text.faqs.4.answer: This tool works with images. For PDFs, first take a screenshot of the page or use our PDF to Word converter to extract text directly from PDF files.
tools.image-to-text.faqs.5.question: Why is the first extraction slow?
tools.image-to-text.faqs.5.answer: The first time you use a language, the OCR model (~5-15 MB) needs to download. After that it's cached in your browser and subsequent extractions are faster.

tools.digital-signature.faqs.0.question: Is this a legally binding signature?
tools.digital-signature.faqs.0.answer: This tool creates a signature image. Legal validity depends on your jurisdiction and the platform accepting the signature. For legally binding e-signatures, you typically need a service that provides an audit trail and identity verification.
tools.digital-signature.faqs.1.question: Can I use this signature on PDFs?
tools.digital-signature.faqs.1.answer: Yes. Download as PNG with transparent background and insert it into any PDF using Preview (Mac), Adobe Reader, or any PDF editor. Most PDF tools have an 'Add Image' or 'Stamp' feature.
tools.digital-signature.faqs.2.question: Is my signature stored anywhere?
tools.digital-signature.faqs.2.answer: No. Everything runs in your browser. Your signature is never uploaded to any server. When you close the page, the signature exists only in your downloaded file.
tools.digital-signature.faqs.3.question: What format should I download?
tools.digital-signature.faqs.3.answer: PNG is best for most uses — it supports transparency so the signature overlays cleanly on documents. SVG is vector format, useful if you need to scale the signature to any size without quality loss.
tools.digital-signature.faqs.4.question: Can I change the color?
tools.digital-signature.faqs.4.answer: Yes. Choose from preset colors including black, navy, and dark red. The color applies to both drawn and typed signatures.
tools.digital-signature.guide.whatIs.tit: What Is the Digital Signature Creator?
tools.digital-signature.guide.whatIs.bod: Create a digital signature image by drawing with your mouse or finger, typing your name in a script font, or uploading an existing signature image. Download the result as a transparent PNG or scalable SVG.

tools.pdf-to-word.guide.steps.1: Click "Convert to Word" to extract text.
tools.pdf-to-word.guide.steps.3: Download as .doc file (opens in Word, Google Docs, LibreOffice).
tools.pdf-to-word.faqs.0.question: How do I convert a PDF to Word for free?
tools.pdf-to-word.faqs.0.answer: Upload your PDF to this tool and click Convert. It extracts all text content and generates a Word-compatible .doc file you can download and edit in Microsoft Word, Google Docs, or LibreOffice.
tools.pdf-to-word.faqs.1.question: Does this preserve PDF formatting?
tools.pdf-to-word.faqs.1.answer: The tool extracts text content with basic paragraph structure. Complex layouts, tables, and images are converted to their text equivalents. For best results with heavily formatted PDFs, consider using desktop software.
tools.pdf-to-word.faqs.2.question: Is my PDF uploaded to a server?
tools.pdf-to-word.faqs.2.answer: No. The entire conversion happens in your browser using PDF.js. Your document never leaves your device — nothing is uploaded, nothing is stored.
tools.pdf-to-word.faqs.3.question: Can I convert scanned PDFs?
tools.pdf-to-word.faqs.3.answer: This tool works with text-based PDFs where text was typed or generated digitally. For scanned PDFs (which are images), you'll need OCR first — try our Image to Text tool to extract text from scanned pages.
tools.pdf-to-word.faqs.4.question: What's the maximum PDF size?
tools.pdf-to-word.faqs.4.answer: There's no hard limit since processing happens locally, but very large PDFs (100+ pages) may take longer and use more memory. For best performance, split large PDFs first using our PDF Splitter.
tools.pdf-to-word.faqs.5.question: Can I convert password-protected PDFs?
tools.pdf-to-word.faqs.5.answer: No. Password-protected PDFs must be unlocked before conversion. Remove the password using the original PDF software or your PDF viewer's security settings.

tools.claude-code-text-formatter.metadat: Clean up messy terminal & Claude Code output. Strip ANSI codes, line numbers, and control characters.
What does the Claude Code Text Formatter do?

It cleans up messy terminal and Claude Code output by removing ANSI escape codes, line numbers, and control characters. The result is plain, readable text that you can copy, paste, and share without the noise.
Will my text be uploaded to a server?
No. Everything runs locally in your browser. Your text never leaves your device, so it's safe for cleaning output that contains sensitive information.
ANSI escape codes are special character sequences that terminals use to add colors and formatting. When you copy terminal output, these codes often appear as raw garbage sequences or invisible control characters. This tool strips them automatically.
Can I keep line numbers in the output?
Line numbers are removed by default. If your output has no line numbers, or you only need to strip ANSI codes, you can turn the Strip Line Numbers option off before formatting.
tools.claude-code-text-formatter.guide.i: What Is the Claude Code Text Formatter?

The Claude Code Text Formatter cleans up messy terminal and Claude Code output by stripping ANSI escape codes, line numbers, and control characters. It turns cluttered CLI output into plain, readable text that you can copy, paste, and share without the noise.
Everything runs locally in your browser. Your input never leaves your device, so the tool is safe for cleaning output that contains sensitive information.
tools.claude-code-text-formatter.guide.s: Cleaning up output takes just a few seconds:
Paste or type your messy text into the Input box.
Choose which elements to strip: ANSI codes, control characters, and line numbers.
Click Format and copy the cleaned result from the Output box.

Terminal tools like Claude Code add ANSI escape codes to colorize text, highlight syntax, and control the cursor. When you copy that output into a plain-text editor, the escape codes are often shown as raw garbage sequences or invisible control characters that break your document.
Line numbers added by terminal multiplexers and log viewers also create extra noise. The formatter removes all of this automatically.
Cleaning Claude Code session logs before sharing them in bug reports.
Copying terminal output into tickets, docs, or chat messages without escape-code noise.
Preparing log snippets for code reviews and documentation.
Removing line numbers from code listings so they can be pasted back into editors.
If a pasted block still looks odd, try toggling Strip Control to remove hidden characters.
The tool handles output from most modern terminals, including iTerm, Windows Terminal, and VS Code's integrated terminal.
There is no limit on input size, so you can clean very long logs in one pass.

tools.fancy-text-generator.faqs.0.questi: How does the fancy text generator work?
tools.fancy-text-generator.faqs.0.answer: It converts your text into special Unicode characters that look like different fonts. These characters are part of the Unicode standard, so they work everywhere that supports Unicode — social media bios, messages, comments, and more.
tools.fancy-text-generator.faqs.1.questi: Can I use fancy text on Instagram, TikTok, and Twitter?
tools.fancy-text-generator.faqs.1.answer: Yes. The generated text uses Unicode characters that work on Instagram bios and captions, TikTok bios, Twitter/X posts, Facebook, YouTube, Discord, and virtually any platform that supports text input.
tools.fancy-text-generator.faqs.2.questi: Why do some characters look different on different devices?
tools.fancy-text-generator.faqs.2.answer: Unicode characters are rendered by each device's font system. Some older devices or browsers may not support all Unicode blocks, which can cause certain styles to display as boxes or question marks. The most widely supported styles are Bold, Italic, and Circled.
tools.fancy-text-generator.faqs.3.answer: There is no limit in this tool. However, keep in mind that some Unicode characters count as 2-4 characters on platforms with character limits (like Twitter's 280 character limit), since they use multi-byte encoding.
tools.fancy-text-generator.faqs.4.answer: No — these are Unicode characters that visually resemble different font styles. Real fonts require CSS or font files. The advantage of Unicode text is that it can be pasted anywhere without any special formatting.

tools.image-compressor.metadata.title: Image Compressor
tools.image-compressor.metadata.descript: Compress images by up to 90% with adjustable quality. No upload, runs in your browser.
tools.image-compressor.faqs.0.question: Does the image compressor work in my browser?
tools.image-compressor.faqs.0.answer: Yes. All compression runs locally in your browser using WebAssembly and the canvas API — PNG uses the oxipng quantizer, GIF uses gifsicle, AVIF uses libavif, and SVG uses svgo. Nothing is uploaded to a server, so your files stay on your device.
tools.image-compressor.faqs.1.question: Which formats are supported?
tools.image-compressor.faqs.1.answer: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF, and SVG. You can also change the output format while compressing, so a bulky PNG can become a small WebP, AVIF, or JPEG in one step.
tools.image-compressor.faqs.2.question: How much can I reduce the file size?
tools.image-compressor.faqs.2.answer: Photos typically compress 50% to 90% as JPEG, WebP, or AVIF. PNG and GIF files gain the most from the color-count and dithering controls, which can shrink them dramatically.
tools.image-compressor.faqs.3.question: What do the Colors and Dithering options do?
tools.image-compressor.faqs.3.answer: Colors sets the palette size for PNG and GIF output (2–256). Fewer colors mean smaller files but a flatter look. Dithering blends adjacent colors to hide banding when the palette is reduced.
tools.image-compressor.faqs.4.question: Can I compress multiple images at once?
tools.image-compressor.faqs.4.answer: Yes. Upload as many images as you like, compress them all at once, and download the results individually or as a single ZIP archive.
tools.image-compressor.guide.intro.title: What Is the Image Compressor?
tools.image-compressor.guide.intro.parag: The Image Compressor shrinks image file sizes by up to 90%. It supports JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF, and SVG, with batch upload, color-count and dithering controls, resizing, and ZIP download. PNG files are compressed with the oxipng quantizer, GIF with gifsicle, AVIF with libavif, and SVG with svgo.
All compression happens in your browser — the WebAssembly engines run in a background worker so the page stays responsive, nothing is uploaded, and your images never leave your device.
Compressing an image takes three steps:
Upload or drop one or more images.
Choose the output format, quality, colors, dithering, and resize options.
Click Compress All and watch the progress.
Compare sizes, then download each image or the whole batch as a ZIP.
JPEG is the best all-around choice for photos. WebP and AVIF offer even better compression for photos and graphics and are supported by all modern browsers. PNG is lossless and ideal for sharp edges, text, or transparency — use the Colors and Dithering controls to shrink it dramatically. GIF suits small animations and logos with flat colors.
Shrinking product photos before uploading them to an online store.
Optimizing images for web pages and email newsletters to speed up loading.
Reducing file size so images fit within messenger and email attachment limits.
Preparing social media images that upload faster on slow connections.
Start at 80% quality — it usually looks identical to the original while saving a lot of space.
For images with transparency, keep PNG and only lower quality if size still matters.
Compress the largest images first; they offer the biggest savings.
Use the format dropdown to convert a bulky PNG to WebP or JPEG in the same step.

tools.image-resizer.metadata.title: Image Resizer
tools.image-resizer.metadata.description: Resize images with social media presets for Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, and more.
tools.image-resizer.faqs.0.question: How do I resize an image?
tools.image-resizer.faqs.0.answer: Upload an image, then either pick a social media preset or enter a custom width and height in pixels. You can also scale by percentage. Maintain aspect ratio keeps the proportions intact so your image isn't stretched.
tools.image-resizer.faqs.1.question: Which formats are supported?
tools.image-resizer.faqs.1.answer: You can upload JPG, PNG, WebP, and other common image formats. The resized result is downloaded as a PNG by default, which preserves quality and transparency.
tools.image-resizer.faqs.2.question: What are the social media presets for?
tools.image-resizer.faqs.2.answer: Presets apply the exact pixel dimensions recommended for Instagram posts (1080x1080), stories (1080x1920), YouTube thumbnails (1280x720), Facebook covers, and more — so you don't have to look up the numbers yourself.
tools.image-resizer.faqs.3.question: Will enlarging a small image make it blurry?
tools.image-resizer.faqs.3.answer: Enlarging an image interpolates new pixels, so the result can look softer or blurry. For best quality, resize images that are already at least as large as the target dimensions.

tools.image-resizer.guide.sections.1.par: The built-in presets cover the most commonly recommended dimensions: Instagram square posts (1080x1080), Instagram stories and Reels (1080x1920), YouTube thumbnails (1280x720), Facebook profile and cover sizes, Twitter/X header images, and Pinterest pins. Selecting a preset automatically fills in the exact width and height for you.
tools.image-resizer.guide.sections.2.par: Aspect ratio is the relationship between an image's width and height. Changing only one dimension breaks the ratio and distorts the image. With Maintain aspect ratio enabled, the resizer scales both dimensions proportionally, and the Aspect Ratio Calculator is available if you need to work out dimensions for a specific ratio like 16:9 or 4:3.
tools.image-resizer.guide.sections.3.ite: Resize before compressing for the smallest final file size.
Use 100% zoom in the preview to check sharpness after resizing.
For print, target at least 300 DPI at the final print size.
Downscaling improves perceived sharpness — it's a great way to clean up large camera photos.

tools.convert.faqs.0.answer: The converter supports 20+ formats including JPG, PNG, WebP, SVG, HEIC, GIF, BMP, TIFF, and ICO. You can convert in any direction between the supported formats.
tools.convert.faqs.1.question: Does the conversion happen on my device?
tools.convert.faqs.1.answer: Yes. Conversion runs entirely in your browser using the canvas API. Your images are never uploaded to a server, which makes the tool fast, free, and private.
tools.convert.faqs.2.question: Will converting reduce the quality of my image?
tools.convert.faqs.2.answer: Conversion to lossless formats like PNG, BMP, and TIFF preserves quality. Converting to lossy formats like JPG applies compression, which trades a small amount of quality for much smaller file sizes.
tools.convert.faqs.3.question: Can I convert multiple images at once?
tools.convert.faqs.3.answer: You can convert images one at a time. Each conversion is instant and requires no waiting or upload, so converting several files is just a matter of repeating the two steps.

tools.convert.guide.intro.paragraphs.0: The Image Format Converter changes an image from one format to another — JPG to PNG, PNG to WebP, HEIC to JPG, SVG to PNG, and 20+ other combinations — in a single click. It's the fastest way to make an image compatible with a website, app, or platform.

tools.convert.guide.sections.1.title: Which Format Should I Use?
tools.convert.guide.sections.1.paragraph: Use JPEG for photos on the web, PNG for graphics with transparency or sharp text, WebP for the best modern web compression, SVG for scalable logos and icons, HEIC only if your target platform supports Apple's format, and ICO for Windows icons. When in doubt, PNG and WebP are safe, widely supported choices.
tools.convert.guide.sections.2.title: Lossless vs. Lossy Conversion
tools.convert.guide.sections.2.paragraph: Converting to PNG, BMP, or TIFF is lossless — every pixel is kept. Converting to JPG applies lossy compression that discards some detail to shrink the file; the higher the compression, the smaller the file and the softer the image. Transparency is lost when converting to JPG, so export PNG or WebP if you need a transparent background.

tools.audio-converter.faqs.0.question: What audio formats can I convert?
tools.audio-converter.faqs.0.answer: You can convert between MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, M4A, OPUS, and AIFF. As input, most common audio files work too, including AAC, WMA, and audio tracks inside WebM containers.
tools.audio-converter.faqs.1.question: Is my audio uploaded anywhere?
tools.audio-converter.faqs.1.answer: No. All conversion happens locally in your browser using FFmpeg WebAssembly. Your audio files never leave your device, so it is safe for voice notes, recordings, and anything sensitive.
tools.audio-converter.faqs.2.question: What is the difference between MP3 and FLAC?
tools.audio-converter.faqs.2.answer: MP3 is a lossy format — it discards some detail to keep files small. FLAC is lossless — it preserves every detail but produces larger files. WAV and AIFF are uncompressed, which gives the largest files of all.
tools.audio-converter.faqs.3.question: Which bitrate should I choose?
tools.audio-converter.faqs.3.answer: For music, use High (256 kbps) or Best (320 kbps) for the best balance of size and quality. For podcasts and voice recordings, Low or Medium is usually indistinguishable from the source.
tools.audio-converter.faqs.4.question: Can I convert without losing quality?
tools.audio-converter.faqs.4.answer: Yes. Choose WAV, FLAC, or AIFF — all three are lossless formats that preserve the original audio quality exactly.
